title: Human Body Systems
description: How the digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems work together to keep us alive.

notes.heading: Digestive System
notes.body: Mouth (chewing + saliva) → oesophagus → stomach (acid + enzymes) → small intestine (absorption via villi) → large intestine (water absorption) → rectum. Enzymes: amylase (starch), protease (protein), lipase (fat).

notes.heading: Circulatory System
notes.body: Heart is a double pump: right side → lungs (pulmonary), left side → body (systemic). Arteries carry blood away (high pressure). Veins carry blood back (low pressure, have valves). Capillaries: gas/nutrient exchange. Red blood cells carry oxygen via haemoglobin.

notes.heading: Respiratory System
notes.body: Air: nose/mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. Alveoli: tiny air sacs with large surface area, thin walls, moist surface, rich blood supply — ideal for gas exchange. O₂ diffuses into blood; CO₂ diffuses out.

flashcards.definition: Biological catalyst that speeds up reactions without being used up.
flashcards.example: Amylase breaks down starch in the mouth.

questions.stem: Where does absorption of digested food mainly occur?
questions.explanation: Small intestine has millions of villi for maximum absorption.

questions.stem: Which enzyme digests starch in the mouth?
questions.explanation: Amylase in saliva begins breaking down starch.

questions.stem: What makes alveoli efficient at gas exchange?
choices: Large surface area, thin walls, good blood supply
questions.explanation: Millions of alveoli with one-cell-thick walls and surrounded by capillaries.

questions.stem: Where does the right side of the heart pump blood?
questions.explanation: Right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.

questions.stem: Which vessel carries blood back to the heart under low pressure?
questions.explanation: Veins return blood to the heart; they have valves to prevent backflow.
